chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Maghra', from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about game struck by an arrow (or projectile), while he had said the name of God at the time of throwing, and he said: 'Eat it if it hits it and he sees it.'

And regarding the game of the Mi'rad (a type of hunting net or trap), he said: 'If he had no other arrows besides it and he said the name of God when throwing, let him eat from it; and if he had other arrows besides it, then no (he should not eat it).'

key_terms.بِحَدِيدَةٍ: With an arrow or sharp projectile
key_terms.سَمَّى: He said (the name of God / Bismillah)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for eating game hunted with arrows or nets in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the conditions for consuming game hunted with projectiles, emphasizing the necessity of reciting God's name at the moment of release and visual confirmation of the hit. It further distinguishes between using a single arrow versus multiple arrows, reflecting the scholarly principle that the specific invocation must be directly linked to the instrument of death to ensure validity.
